chain: 1 hop: local Debian 13 client VM (home internet via a consumer VPN) -> OCI exit (me-dubai-1, VM.Standard.E2.1.Micro, Ubuntu 22.04)
operator: Nitrokey FIDO2 Ed25519 assertion + sealed ML-DSA-65 (one PIN + touch)
exit_protection: none (Ubuntu 22.04 systemd 249 predates systemd-creds); keys generated on the exit, never transferred
defects_found: app-mode DNS leak: nss-resolve and D-Bus reach the host systemd-resolved over Unix sockets, bypassing the app network namespace (fixed: resolver sockets hidden in the app mount namespace; regression test with fake sockets, mutation-checked)

desktop PIN prompt regression: desktop apps run in systemd scopes (INVOCATION_ID set), which diverted the PIN to systemd-ask-password (fixed: desktop before service; regression test, mutation-checked)
hash lock not installable on Python 3.10 (pycparser 3.12 needs >=3.11; typing-extensions needed <3.11) (fixed with version markers; suite passes on 3.10)
binaries built on Debian 13 need glibc 2.38 (built for the exit in an Ubuntu 22.04 container: glibc 2.34)
hosts with a default-drop iptables INPUT/FORWARD (OCI Ubuntu images) also need accepts for the carrier port, avwg0:4433, avpn0:1053 and avpn0 forwarding
not_tested: 2 and 3 hops over the internet (AWS relay pending aws login)
installed boot on the exit host (exit started, not enabled)

two_hop.chain: 2 hops: local client VM (home, via a consumer VPN) -> AWS relay eu-north-1 (t3.micro, Debian 13, UEFI NitroTPM AMI, systemd-creds host+tpm2) -> OCI exit me-dubai-1
two_hop.operator: same Nitrokey operator identity (one PIN + touch)
two_hop.switched_with: enroll --replace on client and exit (device keys kept)
two_hop.captures: taken to /dev/shm (RAM) and deleted after counting sources
defects_found: systemd-creds --with-key=auto silently used the host key when TSS2 libraries were missing (fixed: explicit host+tpm2 when systemd-analyze has-tpm2 passes; recorded in protection.json)
public hop listeners bound the public IP, which 1:1-NAT clouds do not put on the interface (fixed: middle/exit bind 0.0.0.0:<port>)

three_hop.chain: 3 hops: client VM (home) -> AWS relay eu-north-1 (198.51.100.80) -> AWS middle eu-north-1 (198.51.100.82, t3.micro, NitroTPM, keys host+tpm2) -> OCI exit me-dubai-1
three_hop.switched_with: enroll --replace on client, relay and exit; middle enrolled new; device keys kept
three_hop.note: Middle and exit in different providers; relay and middle both AWS for this test.

published_redactions: Public addresses, host names and key fingerprints were replaced with documentation values (RFC 5737) before publication; the measurements are unchanged.
